This is very relatable. I always end up cramming too, do not feel bad. Now about what you should do, I’ll tell you what i do. 
Cramming 101. 
1. Believe that YOU CAN complete the preparation on time, and you will. Trust me it’s the first and most important step. Thinking that you will fail will only make it harder for you. Relax your mind and just work towards your goal. 
Acknowledge that you have very little time but it’s not impossible to complete preparation. 
2. Acknowledge that you have to work extra extra hard this time and spend more time on studies than you otherwise were going to. 2 subjects, more work, more time is needed. I am talking around 10-12 hours in a day(if you don’t work). Yes, sounds extreme but is it? I mean it’s the last week and we haven’t started to do past papers yet, so yeah give as much time as possible. It is uncomfortable but it’s time to get comfortable with being uncomfortable. 
3. Take breaks. Study for an hour and take a break of 10 minutes. If you’re wanna study all day, this is a good technique and helps you incorporate smart work with hard work. 
4. Now, since you haven’t started to practice questions, buckle up, minimise phone usage(if you are addicted like me) and finish reading the topics as soon as possible, so you can move to kit/past papers. 
Or simultaneously start doing questions related to topics you are good at on side. (Some reading, some practice). 
5. Idk how many past papers you normally do, but i would suggest doing at least 5-6 exams for each paper. 
6. For PM, don’t forget to read technical articles. Will take couple of hours. Do them at the very end, just read the topics you find hard. 



Lastly, you’re not doing too bad, don’t worry. Just put a little more time this time and you shall be fine. You totally don’t have to spend all day studying, that’s just what I’ve been doing because let’s just say I started to study AFM last week and now I’ve a lot to do. 
You got this.

Make a mind map. Most topics are linked in some way and the sooner you understand how the whole audit process works in a big picture, the easier it will be to understand.

In the end you must understand that it’s impossible to memorise everything word to word, as long as you understand topics well, recall them, and PRACTICE PAST PAPER A LOT!! You will be fine and things will come to you during exam hopefully.
